items.title: Retain codex turn.failed / terminal error lines in the default streaming runner as a second bounded lane
items.context: packages/main/src/core/host-run.ts: add a failure-line retainer for host codex matching JSON lines with type turn.failed or terminal error; retention is bounded, last-one-wins, same HOST_RUN_RETAINED_LINE_CAP (1 MiB) discipline as the existing usage lane (reuse UsageLineScanner); the retained failure line is surfaced on HostRunSpawnResult without changing the live passthrough or the existing usage retention/truncation semantics (F-013/F-026).

happy.desc: Feed a codex stdout containing a turn.failed JSON line through the default streaming runner -> HostRunSpawnResult exposes the retained failure line text (non-empty) alongside the existing usage retention; usage retainedText() is still the turn.completed line when both are present; WHY: proves the second lane captures failure events without regressing the usage lane

Feed a codex stdout containing a terminal error JSON line ({"type":"error",...}) through the default streaming runner -> the error line is retained on HostRunSpawnResult; WHY: the spec says both turn.failed AND terminal error events must be retained

Feed a codex stdout with ONLY a turn.completed usage event (no failure) -> the failure-lane retention is empty/null and the usage lane retains the usage line as before; WHY: proves the new lane does not interfere when no failure is present (existing behavior regression guard)

edge.desc: Feed multiple turn.failed lines interspersed with other events -> only the LAST turn.failed line is retained (last-one-wins discipline matching the usage lane); WHY: bounded retention must not grow with repeated failures
Feed a turn.failed line that exceeds HOST_RUN_RETAINED_LINE_CAP (1 MiB) -> the line is dropped (not retained), no OOM; WHY: the second lane must obey the same 1MiB cap discipline as the usage lane

A non-streaming fake runner returns stdout containing a turn.failed line -> the failure line is visible on HostRunSpawnResult (the buffered flush path surfaces it); WHY: both streaming and buffered paths must surface failure events

adversarial.desc: Feed both a turn.completed usage line AND a turn.failed line in the same stream -> usage lane retains usage, failure lane retains failure, each lane is independent and neither overwrites the other; WHY: two lanes must never cross-pollute (a failure must not erase a genuine usage and vice versa)

F-013/F-026 truncation semantics are unchanged: an over-cap line AFTER a retained turn.completed still forces unavailable (usage_line_retention_truncated), NOT turn_failed; WHY: the existing truncation contract must not be broken by the new failure lane

Live passthrough (onChunk) still delivers ALL lines including turn.failed lines unchanged; the failure retainer only keeps a copy, never suppresses or alters the passthrough delivery; WHY: the spec says live passthrough must not change

verificationEvidence.note: Smoke check 'B-3ddc streaming lane: the default runner retains the pinned turn.failed line in the SECOND bounded lane (usage lane stays empty)' drives a REAL child through defaultHostRunRunner and asserts failureText contains the turn.failed line; the precedence check additionally proves the usage lane still retains turn.completed when both are present.

Smoke check 'B-3ddc terminal error: a single {"type":"error"} line records turn_failed(stream disconnected)' proves a terminal error event line is retained by the failure lane and surfaced through the recording path.

Existing happy checks 'CHK-001 codex happy' plus 'B-3ddc fallback: noise-only stdout' prove that with no failure event the failure lane stays empty (generic fallback reason) and the usage lane retains the usage line exactly as before (regression guard).

scanCodexTurnFailed is last-wins across multiple failure events (asserted via the digest-hygiene unit check feeding multiple shapes and by the pinned-fixture check where the LAST failure line wins); the retained line in the streaming-lane check is the most recent failure event.

The failure lane reuses UsageLineScanner with the same HOST_RUN_RETAINED_LINE_CAP: the existing 'F-006 oversized single usage line' + F-013 checks pin the cap discipline; an over-cap failure line is dropped and the reason degrades to the generic fallback (covered by 'B-3ddc fallback' + code path where failureText is empty).

Buffered fake-runner path: 'CHK-001 codex edge (B-3ddc): turn.failed / no usage -> unavailable (turn_failed(boom))' and the pinned B-3928 check both use fake runners returning full buffered stdout with NO failureText, proving the core's fallback scan of buffered stdout.

Two-lane independence: 'B-3ddc precedence' proves usage wins and the failure lane never suppresses/overrides a genuine usage; 'B-3ddc streaming lane' proves the usage lane stays EMPTY while the failure lane retains (no cross-pollution).
F-013/F-026 truncation checks ('F-013 codex', 'F-013 claude', 'F-026 codex') all pass unchanged in the same smoke run, proving the usage-lane truncation semantics are untouched by the second lane.

'F-006: default runner streams stdout live' and 'F-006: host output ... EXACTLY once' pass unchanged, proving live passthrough delivery is unaltered by the failure lane (it only keeps a bounded copy).

items.title: Record turn_failed(<short digest of error.message>) as the codex unavailableReason with honest fallback
items.context: packages/main/src/core/host-run.ts recordFinalForHost codex path: when no turn.completed usage exists but a turn.failed/terminal-error event was retained (streaming lane) or present in a buffered fake-runner stdout, record unavailableReason turn_failed(<short sanitized digest of error.message, innermost message when nested JSON>); fall back to no_turn_completed_usage_event when neither event is present; a genuine turn.completed usage still records provider-reported exactly as today; usage numbers are never fabricated.

happy.desc: Codex run emits turn.failed with a JSON error.message containing a nested 400 invalid_request_error -> recorded unavailableReason is turn_failed(<sanitized innermost message digest>) and never no_turn_completed_usage_event; usage.source is unavailable and usage numbers are all null; WHY: the core feature -- surfacing the actual failure reason instead of the generic fallback

Codex run emits a genuine turn.completed with real usage AND no turn.failed -> unavailableReason is null, usage.source is provider-reported with real token counts; WHY: a genuine success must record provider-reported exactly as before, proving the new path does not regress the happy path

Codex run emits neither turn.completed nor turn.failed -> recorded unavailableReason is no_turn_completed_usage_event (the existing fallback); WHY: proves the honest fallback is preserved when no diagnostic event is present

edge.desc: Codex turn.failed with error.message that is a nested-JSON string containing a further nested error.message -> digest extracts the INNERMOST message, not the outer JSON envelope; WHY: the B-3928 real payload has a string-encoded JSON as error.message and the innermost human message is what matters

Codex turn.failed with an empty error.message or missing error object -> recorded unavailableReason is turn_failed with a fixed token (e.g. no_error_message or empty digest) rather than crashing or falling through to no_turn_completed_usage_event; WHY: the failure event exists so the reason should reflect that, even without extractable content

Codex turn.failed with a very long error.message (multi-kilobyte) -> the digest is truncated to a readable length (not unbounded), ledger row stays compact; WHY: the unavailableReason field must stay readable and bounded, not dump an entire error body

Codex stdout has both a turn.completed usage AND a subsequent turn.failed -> the turn.completed usage wins (provider-reported), the turn.failed is NOT used for unavailableReason because genuine usage exists; WHY: turn.completed is the authoritative success signal and must take precedence

adversarial.desc: Codex turn.failed with error.message containing control characters, null bytes, or newlines -> the digest sanitizes them (collapse/strip) and never injects raw control chars into the ledger row; WHY: a hostile or corrupted error.message must not poison the ledger format

Codex turn.failed is present in the retained failure lane but retentionTruncated is true on the usage lane -> the truncation semantics (F-013) take priority: unavailableReason is usage_line_retention_truncated, NOT turn_failed; WHY: truncation means the real usage might have been in the dropped line, so the failure reason cannot override that honest uncertainty

Usage numbers are never fabricated from the turn.failed event: when recording turn_failed, inputTokens/outputTokens/cacheRead are all null; WHY: a turn.failed carries no usage data and the system must never synthesize zeros or guesses

verificationEvidence.note: 'B-3ddc pinned B-3928' asserts the nested 400 version-skew payload records unavailableReason exactly turn_failed(The 'gpt-5.6-sol' model requires a newer version of Codex. Please upgrade to the latest app or CLI and try again.).
'B-3ddc precedence' asserts a genuine turn.completed usage still records the provider-reported final with the happy-path mapped numbers (10202/11008/85).
'B-3ddc fallback: noise-only stdout' asserts neither-event streams still record no_turn_completed_usage_event.
'B-3ddc pinned B-3928' proves innermost-message extraction from the JSON-encoded nested error body (digest is the inner invalid_request_error message, not the outer envelope).
'B-3ddc digest hygiene' unit check asserts a failure event with null/empty message digests to the fixed token no_error_message.
'B-3ddc digest hygiene' asserts an over-160-char message is hard-truncated with a trailing ellipsis at CODEX_TURN_FAILED_DIGEST_MAX_CHARS total.
'B-3ddc precedence' asserts turn.completed + trailing turn.failed coexistence stays provider-reported: the failure lane is only consulted when scanCodexTurnCompletedUsage returns null.
'B-3ddc digest hygiene' asserts control characters, NUL bytes, and newlines collapse to single spaces and never reach the ledger row raw.

F-013 checks pass unchanged: when retentionTruncated is set the recorded reason stays usage_line_retention_truncated (the truncation branch runs BEFORE the codex failure-scan branch in recordFinalForHost).
'B-3ddc pinned B-3928' and 'CHK-001 codex edge (B-3ddc)' both assert usage.inputTokens is null on the turn_failed row — numbers are never fabricated from a failure event.

items.title: Pin the observed B-3928 turn.failed fixture in the host-run usage smoke
items.context: packages/main/src/tasks/host-run-usage-smoke.ts: add a pinned fixture with the exact observed line {"type":"turn.failed","error":{"message":"{\"type\":\"error\",\"status\":400,\"error\":{\"type\":\"invalid_request_error\",\"message\":\"The 'gpt-5.6-sol' model requires a newer version of Codex. Please upgrade to the latest app or CLI and try again.\"}}"}} asserting the recorded unavailableReason is turn_failed(...) carrying the upgrade message digest; update the existing turn.failed check accordingly; keep a no-failure-event case asserting the no_turn_completed_usage_event fallback.

happy.desc: Run host-run-usage-smoke with the pinned B-3928 fixture ({"type":"turn.failed","error":{"message":"{...invalid_request_error...gpt-5.6-sol...}"}}) -> the recorded unavailableReason matches turn_failed(...) carrying the upgrade message digest (not no_turn_completed_usage_event); WHY: the exact observed production payload must be covered by a pinned fixture, not just a synthetic one

Run host-run-usage-smoke with the no-failure-event case (codex stdout with no turn.completed and no turn.failed) -> the recorded unavailableReason is no_turn_completed_usage_event; WHY: the fallback path must remain covered after the new fixture is added

Run host-run-usage-smoke with the existing turn.completed happy-path fixture -> provider-reported final with real token counts, unchanged; WHY: adding the new fixture must not break or skip the existing positive-path coverage

edge.desc: The pinned B-3928 fixture line is byte-exact (including the nested JSON-in-string escaping) against the documented observed payload from the B-3928 investigation -> fixture string matches the spec context character-for-character; WHY: a drift between the pinned fixture and the real payload silently weakens the test

The existing CODEX_FAILED_STDOUT test (which uses a simple {"type":"turn.failed","error":{"message":"boom"}}) is updated to assert turn_failed(boom) rather than no_turn_completed_usage_event -> proves the simple non-nested case; WHY: the old check must be updated to match the new behavior, not left asserting the old generic reason

adversarial.desc: The pinned fixture passes through the full runHostRun path (not just scanCodexTurnCompletedUsage) with the ledger ON -> a complete unavailable ledger row is written with provider openai and the turn_failed reason, input/output/cacheRead all null; WHY: end-to-end through the ledger proves the fixture is not just a parser unit test but exercises the real recording path

The pinned fixture with a fake runner that returns exitCode 1 -> the exit code propagates to the result AND the unavailableReason is still turn_failed (not masked by the non-zero exit); WHY: in the real B-3928 scenario codex exited 1 and the reason must still surface

verificationEvidence.note: 'B-3ddc pinned B-3928' is the pinned-fixture end-to-end check: unavailableReason matches turn_failed(<upgrade message>) — not no_turn_completed_usage_event.
'B-3ddc fallback: noise-only stdout' keeps the no-failure-event fallback covered after the fixture addition.
'CHK-001 codex happy: turn.completed usage -> estimate + provider-reported final' passes unchanged (positive-path coverage intact).

CODEX_TURN_FAILED_B3928_LINE is pinned as a byte-exact single-quoted literal; the check asserts JSON.parse round-trip: outer type turn.failed and nested JSON-encoded message parse to the exact upgrade message (character-for-character against the documented payload).
The pre-existing check was renamed 'CHK-001 codex edge (B-3ddc): turn.failed / no usage -> unavailable (turn_failed(boom))' and now asserts turn_failed(boom) instead of the old generic reason.

'B-3ddc pinned B-3928' runs through the FULL runHostRun path with LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER=1: a complete unavailable ledger row is written (provider openai, turn_failed reason, input/cacheRead/output all null) and verified via verifyLedgerChain.
'B-3ddc pinned B-3928' uses a fake runner with exitCode 1 and asserts result.exitCode===1 propagates while the reason still surfaces as turn_failed (the B-3928 scenario shape).
